clue.text: Place with newspapers found on university hike

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university
Pl. is the abbreviation for Place in street addresses
two papers: the i, a British daily, and the FT, the Financial Times

explanation.surface: A spot where the papers turn up on a student ramble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply tacks the papers on after the place; 'found on' puts the whole lot after the university letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a hike is a rise in prices or wages, and an uplift is the same kind of increase.

clue.text: Silly wind-up does upset

indicators.note: silly suggests letters acting foolishly, out of their sensible order

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A daft prank really annoys someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something upset, like a capsized boat or a knocked-over cup, has been overturned, its top now at the bottom.

clue.text: Colour of apple shown by Monet?

indicators.note: the two neighbouring words, set side by side, show the colour straddling their join

blocks.note: the end of this word
the start of the painter's name

explanation.surface: What shade is the apple in a Monet still life?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that 'shown by' is doing double duty: the painter shows the fruit, and the words placed together show the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon is a pale yellow shade named after the citrus fruit's skin.

clue.text: Collector of food in aid of increasingly old person

blocks.note: to do something for a cause is to do it in aid of it
one who ages, growing older all the time

explanation.surface: Someone gathering food for a charity that helps the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: AGER is a whimsical coinage, someone who ages, rather than a dictionary word.
explanation.definitionFit: A forager searches out and gathers food, as hunter-gatherers or wild-mushroom pickers do.

clue.text: Where people may be caught abroad with some grass

blocks.note: someone abroad is out of the country
a field is an expanse of grass

explanation.surface: Travellers overseas being arrested, perhaps for smoking cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' and 'grass' suggest crime and drugs, but this is cricket: a batter is out caught when a fielder in the outfield takes the ball before it lands.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the outfield is the area far from the pitch where many catches are taken to dismiss batters.

clue.text: Inappropriate French article and a couple from Italy

blocks.note: un is French for 'a'
due is Italian for two

explanation.surface: An unsuitable French newspaper piece and a pair of Italian visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A couple from Italy' reads like two visitors, but it is the Italian word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means excessive or unwarranted, as in undue pressure, so it is out of place or inappropriate.

clue.text: Cut of beef's fine — or Brie crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the preceding letters have gone mad and lost their order

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing between a beef joint and some cheese with crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' looks like biscuits for the Brie, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: The forerib is a prime joint of beef taken from the front of the rib section.

clue.text: Messing about on or close to barge sure is wrong

indicators.note: the close of a word is its very end, so only its final letter is wanted
messing about means fooling around, so these letters are played with and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Insisting that pottering about on or near a canal barge is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Erroneous describes something containing an error, so it is mistaken or wrong.

clue.text: Herb died diseased

blocks.note: d. is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
someone diseased is ill

explanation.surface: A garden plant that wilted and perished from blight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dill is a feathery aromatic plant used as a culinary herb, especially with fish.

clue.text: Chorus splits regarding key

blocks.note: to split something is to part it, so splits are parts
on as in a talk on a topic, meaning about
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A choir divides over which key to sing in.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song is a piece for several voices singing in harmony, the kind of work a chorus performs.

clue.text: Silk Road city — a spot in desert?

indicators.note: in places the preceding pair of items within the word for an arid region

blocks.note: taken as written
a spot or stain is a mark
a desert is a vast stretch of sand

explanation.surface: Is this famous trade-route city just a speck in the desert?
explanation.definitionFit: Samarkand, in modern Uzbekistan, was a major trading city on the ancient Silk Road between China and the West.

clue.text: Two rivers in the country

blocks.note: first river: R, the abbreviation for river
second river: the Ural, which flows through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A pair of rivers flowing through countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things in the country, away from towns and cities.

clue.text: I want you to understand it may be men got Ted

blocks.note: surface reading: a speaker anxious not to be misunderstood

blocks.clueFragment: it may be men got Ted
blocks.note: setter's reading: the letters of the first three words of the answer, put in the wrong order, can make the words men got Ted

explanation.surface: Someone explaining a confusing remark about some men catching Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse anagram: the answer's last word is the shuffle signal, and the three words before it are the fodder that 'men got Ted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said before a remark to stop the listener taking it the wrong way, so it means I want you to understand.

clue.text: Expense relating to teeth after incisors half removed

indicators.note: half removed means the back half of the word is taken away
after sends the phrase before it to the back, so the teeth word comes second

blocks.note: front cutting teeth
dental means relating to teeth

explanation.surface: A dentist's bill after having some front teeth taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Incidentals are minor extra costs, so an incidental is a small additional expense.

clue.text: Prevent crime writer dropping The Times

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so a letter falls out of the name

blocks.note: Colin Dexter, author of the Inspector Morse novels
x is the multiplication sign, read as 'times'

explanation.surface: A crime novelist gets dropped by the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' looks like the newspaper hosting this puzzle, but it is the times sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage or stop them doing something, so it means prevent.

clue.text: Classic play has to contend with most of these around it

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is lost
around means the shortened word goes on either side of the verb

blocks.note: to rival is to compete with
taken as written

explanation.surface: A classic stage work has to compete with most modern plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rivals is Sheridan's 1775 comedy of manners, a classic of the English stage.

clue.text: Pretentious type of word common in Old Norse

indicators.note: in places the preceding words inside the abbreviation for the language

blocks.note: a verb is a part of speech
common in the sense of vulgar or low-class
ON is the standard abbreviation for Old Norse

explanation.surface: A kind of grand word frequently found in Old Norse.
explanation.definitionFit: Overblown describes something inflated and pompous, so it means pretentious.

clue.text: Right work in hospital department in charge of rising disorder?

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: entropic means marked by increasing disorder

indicators.note: in places the opening pair of items within the department and charge abbreviations

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
op. is the abbreviation for opus, a work
ENT is ear, nose and throat
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: The proper work in a hospital department responsible for growing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Entropy is the physicists' measure of disorder, which always tends to increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Entropic means relating to entropy, the measure of disorder that in a closed system keeps rising.

clue.text: Certainly not Falstaff for Thursday evening perhaps

blocks.note: Falstaff is Shakespeare's famously fat knight, so whoever is certainly not him is tiny
Sir John Falstaff holds that rank

explanation.surface: Choosing someone other than the jovial Falstaff for a Thursday night show.
explanation.walkthrough: Wee is Scottish for small: the whole phrase stands for a little knight, the opposite of the enormous Falstaff.
explanation.definitionFit: Thursday is a working day, so its evening is an example of a weeknight, one not falling at the weekend.

clue.text: Streamlined fairing's new, with excellent lines on plane's tail

indicators.note: the tail is the very end, so only the final letter is taken

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
ace means excellent
l is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural
its final letter

explanation.surface: An aircraft's new streamlined casing gets top-quality lines at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined housing round an aircraft engine, a kind of fairing.

clue.text: Girl going short without hot eastern food

indicators.note: going short means getting shorter, so the name loses its last letter
without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened name goes around

blocks.note: a girl's name
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A girl going hungry with no hot Asian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the older sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, food from the Far East.

clue.text: Small lock and key finally oiled?

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter is wanted

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a lock of hair styled up at the front
its final letter

explanation.surface: A little lock and key that may need lubricating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oiled' is British slang for drunk, and squiffy is a jokey word for slightly tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Squiffy means slightly drunk, and well-oiled or oiled is a slang term for the same.

clue.text: Is jazz band mostly rubbish in engagement upset?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
in places the earlier words inside the word for an engagement

blocks.note: taken as written
a combo is a small jazz group
bull is slang for nonsense
a date is an appointment or engagement

explanation.surface: Asking whether a poor jazz group playing a gig is troubled.
explanation.definitionFit: To discombobulate is a jocular word for to confuse or disconcert, that is, to upset.

clue.text: Amplifier initially made a signal very clipped at both ends

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its first letter
trimmed at front and back, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: its first letter
its first letter
its first letter
its inner letters

explanation.surface: An amplifier that first produced a heavily truncated signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A maser amplifies microwaves by stimulated emission, the forerunner of the laser.

clue.text: Strange fiction in article

indicators.note: in places the untruth within the short article

blocks.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An odd piece of made-up writing in a magazine article.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means foreign or unfamiliar, hence strange.

clue.text: Pine resin has the top left off

indicators.note: with its top left off, the word's first letter in this down clue is omitted

blocks.note: pitch is a dark resin or tar

explanation.surface: A tree whose resin has had the top cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the tree yielding resin; it is the verb meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to long for it, as to pine is.

clue.text: Scent hard work writing out a verse

indicators.note: writing something out of a text removes it

blocks.note: travail is painful toil
taken as written
v is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: A tracker dog laboriously following a scent while a poet works on a stanza.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is the scent or track left by an animal for hounds to follow.

clue.text: Cheeseparer has to strip surface from something hard

blocks.note: to skin something is to strip its outer layer
flint is a very hard stone

explanation.surface: A cheesemaker's tool peeling the rind off something tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeseparer' reads as a kitchen gadget, but it is an old word for a stingy person, one who would pare the rind thin.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeseparer is a mean, penny-pinching person, which is exactly what a skinflint is.

clue.text: Shortly drunk outside English pub

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger about out of their proper order
outside means the shuffled word wraps around the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Soon an Englishman will be drunk outside the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostelry is a jocular or old-fashioned word for an inn or pub.

clue.text: Prince introducing odd extracts from Yemeni songbook

indicators.note: odd extracts are the letters in the first, third and fifth places
introducing means bringing something inside, here into the prince

blocks.note: Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare
its odd-placed letters

explanation.surface: A prince bringing in some songs from Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns, a songbook for church use.
